narrative_purpose: Show metallurgy without a furnace. The fire sits beside the work rather than under it, because the metal is being hammered cold and only warmed enough to soften the damage hammering does.
subject: A curved rectangular plate of pale grey human aircraft alloy, roughly forearm-length, braced flat on a dark stone anvil. Its surface carries a dense field of overlapping shallow hammer dents, and one long edge has been ground down to a straight bevel. A long blue-skinned Na'vi hand grips a rounded stone hammer above it, mid-stroke. To the RIGHT of the anvil, clearly separate from it, sits a low open stone hearth holding a bed of dull orange charcoal with no flames — the metal plate is NOT above or inside it.
scene: A sheltered work area on grey volcanic ground at dusk, a coil of leather cord and two smaller scraps of salvaged alloy nearby, the background deep indigo shadow.
camera: Close three-quarter working view looking down at the anvil, taking in the plate, the hand and the separate hearth beside it.
light: The charcoal bed gives a soft warm glow from the right, raking across the dented plate so the hammer marks catch the light; the rest of the scene sits in cool indigo dusk shadow.
palette: Cool grey alloy and dark stone dominant, deep indigo shadow, a restrained ember-orange glow from the charcoal bed on the right and its warm reflection along the plate.
style: Painterly naturalist plate of a craft in progress, workmanlike and specific.
detail_level: High on the hammered surface of the plate, the ground bevel, the stone hammer and the charcoal bed; the background soft.
composition: Anvil and plate occupying the left two thirds, the separate hearth in the lower right, a broad area of plain dark background at the upper left kept clear for overlaid callouts.
consistency_notes: CRITICAL: the metal is COLD — pale grey, never glowing, never red-hot, never molten. The charcoal bed is beside the work, not under it, and shows no flames. This is cold-hammering and gentle annealing, not smithing. No furnace, bellows or crucible anywhere in the frame.
